history.summary: A 1967 Tiong Bahru SIT walk-up flat on a 99-year lease from 1967 — roughly 40 years of lease remaining — gazetted for conservation in 2003, so no en-bloc is possible. At $1.15M / $1319 PSF for a depreciating, hard-to-finance ~40yr-lease walk-up, this is a heritage/own-stay piece, not an investment.
history.rating_rationale: The 99yr lease from 1967 leaves ~40 years — banks cap LTV and tenor on sub-60yr leases, shrinking the buyer pool and guaranteeing lease-decay drag on price. Conservation gazette removes any en-bloc upside. Walk-up (no lift), no facilities, 780m to MRT. Score 340/1000 and 164-253 arena record confirm a weak technical case. Lease decay over a 5-7yr hold works directly against capital appreciation.
red_flags: ~40 years lease remaining — financing restricted, accelerating lease decay
1967 build, walk-up, no facilities — high maintenance, narrow buyer pool
No URA data; very weak score 340
catalysts: Tiong Bahru heritage charm appeals to a niche own-stay/lifestyle buyer
Central D03 location near Greater Southern Waterfront

agent_evaluation.rental_assessment: Tiong Bahru is rentable to lifestyle tenants, but a walk-up with no facilities commands a discount and a sub-40yr lease limits the eventual exit.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_assessment: Negative bias from lease decay on a ~40yr leasehold with no en-bloc escape; conservation status caps redevelopment value. Expect erosion, not appreciation, over the hold.
